# Claude Code Configuration

Personal Claude Code configuration for Omri Ariav.

## Structure
- `agents/` → local agents (pr-reviewer)
- `commands/` → local slash commands (memory, claude-pulse)
- `skills/` → symlinks into personal repos under ~/Code (per-repo)
- `hooks/` → custom validation hooks
- `settings.json` → plugin configuration
- `claude_desktop_config.json` → MCP servers (Desktop app)

## Plugins (personal + public only; see new-mac/05-claude.sh for the install list)
- omri-marketplace: copy, coacher, find-session, natbag, x
- amq-squad, gws (workspace-cli), personal-memory, claude-mem, codex
- avivsinai-marketplace: amq-cli, bkt, yoetz
- document-skills (Anthropic), frontend-design, vercel
- statusline: claude-pulse (installed with /setup-pulse)

See settings.json for full configuration.

## Outbound message rule (always)
Any email, Slack, or Google Chat message I draft on Omri's behalf MUST end with a final line:

```
Sent by Claude on behalf of Omri
```

This signature is mandatory on every drafted message across all channels. Separately: do NOT auto-send outbound messages — draft and let Omri send, unless he explicitly authorizes a send and confirms the exact text + recipient.

## Slack thread reply rule (always)
When replying in a Slack thread to a specific person, ALWAYS tag them with `<@USER_ID>` at the top of the reply (or naturally within the first sentence). Thread participants are NOT auto-notified on replies — without an explicit mention, the message only reaches them if they happen to be watching the thread. This applies to every directed reply, not just the first one in a thread. If the reply is a general thread update not aimed at any one person, no tag is needed.

## Personal Memory (always)
Long-horizon memory lives in the personal-memory store at `~.a/Code/omri-mem`
(local RAG; replaces the retired pm-os capture/recall flow).

- **Capture**: `memory add …` via the global `memory` wrapper (never hand-write
  `memory/entries/` or `.index/`). Slash: `/remember`.
- **Recall**: `memory recall "<q>"` — ground people/history answers in the store,
  cite entry paths. Slash: `/recall`.
- **Graphs**: one DEFAULT graph (`memory/` — private, home of every capture)
  plus named shared graphs under `memory-graphs/<slug>/`. Capture always lands
  in the default graph. Entries reach a shared graph only via standing
  distribution rules, the promotion review (`/promote --to <graph>`), or an
  explicit user request; membership changes go ONLY through
  `memory copy|move <id> --to <graph>`, never by moving files. Single-graph
  recall: `/recall-graph <graph>`. Graph admin: `/manage-graphs`.
  (The old private/public two-graph model and `/promote-public`,
  `/recall-public` commands are retired.)
- **Publishable staging**: the `public` graph holds source material approved
  for outbound use. When drafting comms/posts/decks from memory, recall from
  it ONLY (`/recall-graph public`) — never ground outbound drafts in private
  memories. Tag a capture `shareable` to auto-copy it there (standing rule);
  backlog enters via `/promote --to public`. Omri still approves every send.
- **English storage policy**: entry bodies are written in English regardless of
  source language; short Hebrew quotes allowed inline. Hebrew questions are
  translated and passed as an extra phrasing to `memory recall`.
- **Show-before-add**: for decisions, feedback, hiring, or anything about a
  person, show Omri the proposed entry body before running `memory add`.
- **Slug discipline**: one person = one kebab slug, forever. Check
  `memory slugs list --kind person` before inventing one.
- **Ambiguous first names**: if a mentioned first name matches more than one
  known slug (e.g. Dana = dana-magen (PA) / dana-nadler (recruiter)) and the
  context does not clearly settle it, ASK Omri instead of guessing — a wrong
  person attribution is silent and poisons person-filtered recall.

</project_instructions>
</project_context>

# Claude Code Configuration

Personal Claude Code configuration for Omri Ariav.

## Structure
- `agents/` → local agents (pr-reviewer)
- `commands/` → local slash commands (memory, claude-pulse)
- `skills/` → symlinks into personal repos under ~/Code (per-repo)
- `hooks/` → custom validation hooks
- `settings.json` → plugin configuration
- `claude_desktop_config.json` → MCP servers (Desktop app)

## Plugins (personal + public only; see new-mac/05-claude.sh for the install list)
- omri-marketplace: copy, coacher, find-session, natbag, x
- amq-squad, gws (workspace-cli), personal-memory, claude-mem, codex
- avivsinai-marketplace: amq-cli, bkt, yoetz
- document-skills (Anthropic), frontend-design, vercel
- statusline: claude-pulse (installed with /setup-pulse)

See settings.json for full configuration.

## Outbound message rule (always)
Any email, Slack, or Google Chat message I draft on Omri's behalf MUST end with a final line:

```
Sent by Claude on behalf of Omri
```

This signature is mandatory on every drafted message across all channels. Separately: do NOT auto-send outbound messages — draft and let Omri send, unless he explicitly authorizes a send and confirms the exact text + recipient.

## Slack thread reply rule (always)
When replying in a Slack thread to a specific person, ALWAYS tag them with `<@USER_ID>` at the top of the reply (or naturally within the first sentence). Thread participants are NOT auto-notified on replies — without an explicit mention, the message only reaches them if they happen to be watching the thread. This applies to every directed reply, not just the first one in a thread. If the reply is a general thread update not aimed at any one person, no tag is needed.

## Personal Memory (always)
Long-horizon memory lives in the personal-memory store at `~.a/Code/omri-mem`
(local RAG; replaces the retired pm-os capture/recall flow).

- **Capture**: `memory add …` via the global `memory` wrapper (never hand-write
  `memory/entries/` or `.index/`). Slash: `/remember`.
- **Recall**: `memory recall "<q>"` — ground people/history answers in the store,
  cite entry paths. Slash: `/recall`.
- **Graphs**: one DEFAULT graph (`memory/` — private, home of every capture)
  plus named shared graphs under `memory-graphs/<slug>/`. Capture always lands
  in the default graph. Entries reach a shared graph only via standing
  distribution rules, the promotion review (`/promote --to <graph>`), or an
  explicit user request; membership changes go ONLY through
  `memory copy|move <id> --to <graph>`, never by moving files. Single-graph
  recall: `/recall-graph <graph>`. Graph admin: `/manage-graphs`.
  (The old private/public two-graph model and `/promote-public`,
  `/recall-public` commands are retired.)
- **Publishable staging**: the `public` graph holds source material approved
  for outbound use. When drafting comms/posts/decks from memory, recall from
  it ONLY (`/recall-graph public`) — never ground outbound drafts in private
  memories. Tag a capture `shareable` to auto-copy it there (standing rule);
  backlog enters via `/promote --to public`. Omri still approves every send.
- **English storage policy**: entry bodies are written in English regardless of
  source language; short Hebrew quotes allowed inline. Hebrew questions are
  translated and passed as an extra phrasing to `memory recall`.
- **Show-before-add**: for decisions, feedback, hiring, or anything about a
  person, show Omri the proposed entry body before running `memory add`.
- **Slug discipline**: one person = one kebab slug, forever. Check
  `memory slugs list --kind person` before inventing one.
- **Ambiguous first names**: if a mentioned first name matches more than one
  known slug (e.g. Dana = dana-magen (PA) / dana-nadler (recruiter)) and the
  context does not clearly settle it, ASK Omri instead of guessing — a wrong
  person attribution is silent and poisons person-filtered recall.

</project_instructions>
</project_context>
